solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Film many despicable folk

parts.note: scum is the film or layer of dirt that forms on the surface of a liquid
bags, as in 'bags of time', means lots or many

explanation.surface: A cinema review dismissing a film as being about a crowd of contemptible people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Film' looks like a cinema film but is a surface layer on a liquid.
explanation.definitionFit: Scumbags is a slang insult for contemptible, worthless people.

clue.text: Boisterously enthusiastic reunion at home initially, repeated

indicators.note: repeated says the three opening letters are written down a second time
initially asks for the opening letter of each of the words reunion, at and home

explanation.surface: A family reunion at home turns into a loud, cheering celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: Rah-rah describes noisy, cheerleading-style enthusiasm, from the cheer 'rah' used at American sports games.

clue.text: Very little to see up in Brooklyn, I think

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the hidden letters are read from bottom to top, backwards
in signals letters lying inside the run of words Brooklyn, I think

explanation.surface: Someone guessing there is hardly anything to see in Brooklyn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' picks YNIT out of BrooklYN I Think, and 'up' turns it round, as the entry is a down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiny is a plain synonym for very small or very little.

clue.text: Two runs are so long!

indicators.note: two asks for two copies of the single cricket run word

parts.note: in cricket a bye is a run scored when the ball passes the batter without being hit

explanation.surface: A cricket commentator signing off after a couple of runs.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a bye is an extra run scored when the ball beats both batter and wicketkeeper; two of them make the farewell.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are casual ways of saying farewell or goodbye to someone leaving.

clue.text: Protesting vehemently, Pam ruins rambles

indicators.note: rambles suggests wandering about aimlessly, so the letters of Pam ruins are rearranged

explanation.surface: Pam angrily objects that her ruins are being trampled by walkers.
explanation.definitionFit: To be up in arms is an idiom for being angry and protesting strongly.

clue.text: Brand new university students meeting press chief

parts.note: NUS is the National Union of Students, the UK student body
the editor heads a newspaper, abbreviated ED

explanation.surface: New university students are introduced to the head of the college press.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unused has never been worn or handled, so it is still in mint condition.

clue.text: It follows itch: pulse dropping regularly

indicators.note: dropping regularly means every other letter of itch and pulse is discarded, keeping the rest

explanation.surface: A medical note: an itch is followed by a weakening, irregular pulse.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the first, third and so on of ITCHPULSE to leave the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters.
explanation.definitionFit: In argument, the word marks a conclusion: therefore, consequently, it follows.

clue.text: Being kind of racy, hit condemned

indicators.note: condemned suggests something wrecked or written off, so the letters of racy and hit are broken up and reset

explanation.surface: A racy hit show is condemned by critics as a certain kind of thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Charity is kindness and generosity shown towards others, a virtue of benevolence.

clue.text: Steal a little salt?

definitions.meaning: slang for stealing or nicking something
the small amount held between finger and thumb, as of salt in cooking

explanation.surface: A cook asks whether to nick a dash of salt.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to filch something and a tiny quantity taken between the fingers.

clue.text: English Catholic overwhelmed by the writer's compassion

indicators.note: overwhelmed by means the English Catholic letters are swamped, sitting inside the possessive word

parts.note: the writer is the setter, so the writer's means my
RC stands for Roman Catholic

explanation.surface: The writer's English Catholic character is overwhelmed by compassion.
explanation.definitionFit: Mercy is compassion or forgiveness shown to someone in one's power.

clue.text: Rewards, perhaps, on boarding public transport

indicators.note: boarding means getting on board, so the little word sits inside the vehicles

parts.note: buses are a common form of public transport

explanation.surface: Commuters are perhaps rewarded for getting on buses.
explanation.definitionFit: Bonuses are extra payments given as rewards, though 'perhaps' admits rewards can take other forms.

clue.text: Irate hack dealt out a punishing blow

indicators.note: dealt out suggests cards distributed and mixed, so the letters of Irate hack are rearranged

explanation.surface: An angry journalist hands out a painful clout.
explanation.definitionFit: A cuff round the head that leaves the ear swollen is the traditional British punishment slap.

clue.text: Moan old ship's appearing where you'd expect vehicles

parts.note: to carp is to complain or moan
Noah's ark is the old ship, so old ship's gives ark's, written ARKS

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles that an old ship turns up where cars ought to be.
explanation.definitionFit: Car parks are places set aside for parking motor cars, so that is where cars are found.

clue.text: Rules you should follow? Endless medicine!

indicators.note: endless means the final letter of the medicine word is cut off

parts.note: a dose is a measured quantity of medicine

explanation.surface: A patient complains about the rules of an unending course of medicine.
explanation.walkthrough: As in 'dos and don'ts', the things you ought to do; the question mark flags the loose definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The dos in 'dos and don'ts' are the instructions or practices one is advised to keep.

clue.text: Posters framing quiet people splashing cash?

indicators.note: framing means the posting word goes round the quiet letter like a frame round a picture

parts.note: posters here are people who post letters, so senders
P is piano, the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: Billboards surround people who are throwing their money about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Posters' looks like printed placards, but means those who post things.
explanation.definitionFit: Spenders are people who part freely with their money, as in 'big spenders'.

clue.text: Firm prepared collection

definitions.meaning: firm or solid, as of jelly that has hardened
a ... is a group of matching items, like a chess ...

explanation.surface: A company has a range of goods ready.
explanation.definitionFit: The one short word covers hardened, ready to go, and a group of things belonging together.

clue.text: Lumberjack's warning doctor to get in line

indicators.note: to get in places the doctor's letters inside the row word

parts.note: a tier is a row or line, as of seats
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A lumberjack warns a doctor to join the queue.
explanation.definitionFit: Woodcutters shout this as a falling tree comes down, to warn people nearby.

clue.text: Shakes exposed, tailless reptile

parts.note: to rock is to shake or sway

indicators.note: tailless means the final letter of the bare word is lost

parts.note: naked means exposed or uncovered

explanation.surface: Someone trembles at the sight of an uncovered reptile with no tail.
explanation.definitionFit: The rock snake is a python of Asia and Africa, a type of reptile.

clue.text: Most retiring, indeed, when in bed

indicators.note: when in puts the word for indeed inside the word for bed

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
yes and indeed both express agreement

explanation.surface: Someone is at their shyest when they are in bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Retiring here means shy or bashful, so the superlative is the shyest.

clue.text: Purposeless, disorganised raid on newspaper

indicators.note: disorganised says the letters of raid are thrown into a muddle

parts.note: FT is the Financial Times, a British newspaper

explanation.surface: A badly planned police raid on a newspaper office achieves nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Drifting without direction or aim, adrift means lacking a clear purpose.

clue.text: Brief account describing July weather, perhaps, hopefully heard!

indicators.note: heard tells us the word for the July weather is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: summery describes warm sunny weather, which July, perhaps, will hopefully bring

explanation.surface: A weather report for July, hoping for sunshine.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain July weather is only 'hopefully' warm, hence the hedging words.
explanation.definitionFit: A summary is a short statement of the main points of something.

clue.text: Band ultimately ignores a request for silence

indicators.note: ultimately asks for the final letter of the word ignores

parts.note: sh is said to ask for quiet

explanation.surface: A music group finally ignores a call to be quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Band' looks like a group of musicians but is a strip of cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: A sash is a long strip of cloth worn round the waist or over the shoulder.

clue.text: Dismissed, if turning communist

indicators.note: turning means the little word if is turned round

parts.note: red is a common label for a communist

explanation.surface: Someone sacked for becoming a communist.
explanation.definitionFit: To be fired is to be sacked from a job.

clue.text: Mild expletive from female on edge

parts.note: a lip is a rim or edge, as of a cup

explanation.surface: A woman on the brink lets slip a gentle swear word.
explanation.definitionFit: Flip is a dated British exclamation of annoyance, a gentle substitute for stronger words.

clue.text: Dot's son getting a quick kiss

parts.note: a peck is a light, brief kiss

explanation.surface: A mother named Dot gets a brief kiss from her boy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dot' reads as a woman's name but is the definition; 's is 'is', the link.
explanation.definitionFit: A speck is a tiny spot or particle, much like a dot.

clue.text: Ferns, if rotten, something that smells

indicators.note: rotten suggests something decayed and spoiled, so the letters of Ferns and if are reworked

explanation.surface: Rotting ferns give off an odour, if anything does.
explanation.definitionFit: A sniffer, like a sniffer dog, is one that detects things by scent.
